# Diffusing DeBias (NeurIPS 2025)

> Diffusing DeBias: Synthetic Bias Amplification for Model Debiasing. Massimiliano Ciranni, Vito Paolo Pastore, Roberto Di Via, Enzo Tartaglione, Francesca Odone, Vittorio Murino (MaLGa-DIBRIS, University of Genoa; AI for Good (AIGO), Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia; Télécom Paris; University of Verona). Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38 (NeurIPS 2025), pp. 116778-116805, DOI 10.52202/085713-3893.

Diffusing DeBias (DDB) is a plug-in for unsupervised model debiasing in image classification. A class-conditional diffusion model with classifier-free guidance is trained on the biased training set and used to generate synthetic bias-aligned images, which fully replace the real training set for training a Bias Amplifier. Since the Bias Amplifier never sees real data, it cannot memorize the scarce bias-conflicting training samples. The Bias Amplifier is plugged into a two-step recipe (Recipe I, pseudo-groups for GroupDRO) and an end-to-end recipe (Recipe II, LfF-style loss-based reweighting).

Key results (mean over three runs):
- Waterbirds: 91.56% worst-group accuracy (DDB-II), above all unsupervised methods and the supervised GroupDRO (91.40%).
- BAR: 72.81% average accuracy (DDB-II), 2.93 points above DebiAN.
- BFFHQ: 74.67% bias-conflicting accuracy (DDB-I) vs. 73.60% for ETF-Debias.
- ImageNet-9/A: 39.80% average accuracy on ImageNet-A (DDB-I).
- UrbanCars (multiple shortcuts): DDB-I gaps of 1.85 (BG), 0.52 (CoObj) and 0.12 (BG+CoObj).
- A Bias Amplifier trained on real Waterbirds data instead memorizes all bias-conflicting samples (50 epochs) or reaches only 79.43% WGA (1 epoch, Recipe I).
- On unbiased CIFAR-10, DDB gives 84.16% vs. 83.26% for ERM.
